section: 29. Final Preparations: Rent a Car for Evacuation
description: Look for a car rental shop, arrange for a translator, keep combat-ready members at the restaurant, make all preparations for the final operation

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: (What do you mean you're not allowed to take it and run? The statue is right there. If you want to take it and run, go ahead. You'll win.)

conversation.text: "Hello, boss. Two coffees, please."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: They chose a seat by the window. Through the foggy glass, they could see Blackshirts changing guard at the opera house entrance. The new guards were stricter than the night shift, even inspecting every layer of canvas on bread delivery trucks.

conversation.speaker: player2

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "By the way, sir, what's going on at the theater? The checks are so strict."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Two coffees and four paninis, coming right up! The boss replied without looking up, the sizzle of frying meat coming from the kitchen behind him. In less than five minutes, the waiter served breakfast—two cups of thick espresso that could stand on a spoon, and a small mountain of panini sandwiches. The bread was golden and crispy, filled with melting cheese and Parma ham, the aroma enticing.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Order a cappuccino

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Just as Bailan was about to ask about the situation, and player2 wanted to order a cappuccino, the cafe doorbell suddenly rang urgently. Three young men in black shirts barged in. The leader walked straight to the counter and slapped a notice on the table: All customers must register their IDs today!

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Check the situation

conversation.speaker: player3

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Johnson obediently handed over his ID, stealing a glance at the defenses outside—behind the machine gun positions, two armored vehicles were parked, with searchlights mounted on their roofs. More alarming was the sniper glint on the opera house roof; at least three firing points covered all approach paths. The grenades on the Blackshirts' belts clinked as they moved. This wasn't regular security; it was like preparing for war. Suddenly, the cafe radio broadcast the morning news: ...Police announced a ban on any gatherings within 500 meters of La Scala Opera House today...

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: The problem is how to get it out.)

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The three Blackshirts plopped down at the next table, their weapons clattering to the floor. "Damn guard duty..." a young man muttered to his companions in a low voice.

They say that big shot's stomach..." The third guard's cough suddenly interrupted the conversation as he tapped his companion's boot with his rifle butt. The three fell silent simultaneously.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: When the Blackshirts finally left the café, the investigators quickly moved toward the theater. However, as soon as they approached the square, a piercing whistle cut through the air. Halt! Restricted area! Six armed guards instantly surrounded them, pressing gun barrels directly against the investigators' chests. The leading officer coldly flipped open an ID booklet: Non-staff are prohibited from entering eight hours before the performance.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #Take out the pass

conversation.speaker: player5

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: At that moment, the large clock struck eight, and a broadcast sounded: All staff of Aida, please report to the east gate for medical examination... At the end of the line, actors were having blood samples drawn by people in white coats, their arms bare.

conversation.speaker: player4
conversation.text: "Hmm?"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: After carefully inspecting the pass, the officer reluctantly waved his hand: Go in, don't get in the way. Also, if you dare approach the backstage, we'll shoot you.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: Hiss...

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: A temporary tent was set up in front of the east gate, where two doctors in white coats were measuring temperature and blood pressure. Actors in the line yawned, and someone muttered quietly: They do this every opening night...

conversation.speaker: player5

conversation.text: Blackshirts stand guard in groups of three at every passage, pistols and batons at their waists. Two guards with rifles stand on each side of the stage, muzzles angled downward, fingers on the triggers.

conversation.text: #Prepare to head to the prop room first

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: On the second-floor box area, the silhouettes of two snipers are faintly visible. At the staircase leading to the basement stands an officer, flipping through something, a snarling military dog lying at his feet.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "We need to go take a look at the stage area"

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "There's a white headless statue"

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Louisa frowned and looked up: A white headless statue? She flicked her cigarette ash; that thing is to be used as an armor stand on stage. Didn't I tell you all about it yesterday?

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: "But it seems that thing was sold when we checked the accounts yesterday."

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Louisa impatiently brushed the stray hairs from her forehead: Accounts? That stuff has been a mess for ages. She kicked a wooden crate at her feet; last week when moving props, we even found three unnumbered Egyptian statues extra. When we took inventory before leaving work yesterday, that white statue was still standing perfectly fine on the stage wing.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: "Leave moving it to us."

conversation.speaker: player12
conversation.text: "Hey! Coming right up!" #gets to work quickly and efficiently

conversation.text: Louisa and the prop crew efficiently moved Prop Number Seven—Radames's full set of golden armor and costume—onto a cart. The armor gleamed under the lights.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #helps teammates move the armor over

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The investigators pushed the armor through the dimly lit corridor to the stage backstage. It was busy and noisy here; actors were making final preparations, makeup artists chased extras for touch-ups, and prop masters shuttled back and forth moving scenery.

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #lightly quickens pace, but without losing any caution, treating this escort task with the depth, meticulousness, and patience of archaeology.

conversation.speaker: player2
conversation.text: #quickly follows

conversation.speaker: player5
conversation.text: #goes to the place described in the companion's memory, looking for that white headless statue.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Bailan carefully searched through the pile of props on the west side of the stage and finally found the target behind a stack of golden shields and fake palm trees—that white headless statue. It was casually leaning against the corner of the wall.
